title: Introduce anchored semantic token ramps and micro-elevation shadow system for dense components
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: our current token set is inconsistent across density modes (compact/regular), produces unpredictable contrast at small sizes, and lacks a fine-grained elevation system for dense tables and charts. This causes visual noise in analytics UIs and makes accessibility QA brittle.

Goal: deliver a cohesive token update that introduces: anchored semantic color ramps (neutral and accent anchors), a proportional typography rebaseline for small-form-factor data surfaces, a spacing/radius axis tuned for dense rows, and a 5-step micro-elevation (shadow) system that maps directly to z-index and interactive press depths.

What we will change:
- Define semantic anchors (neutral-0, neutral-50, neutral-100, accent-anch0) with explicit contrast deltas rather than absolute hex swaps. Anchors will be used to generate derived ramps for light/dark and compact modes.
- Add a compact typography scale: micro (10), small (12), body (14) with updated line-height and token aliases so components can opt into compact scales without breaking spacing.
- Introduce a spacing axis (space-xs, space-sm, space-md, space-lg) for density-aware components. Compact components override aliases to a denser mapping.
- Replace ad-hoc radius values with an axis-based radius tokenset (radius-0, radius-1, radius-2) and guidelines for which components use which level in dense layouts.
- Establish micro-elevation tokens (elevation-0 .. elevation-4) with precise shadow layers, alpha stops, and recommended use-cases (hover / focus / pressed / modal micro-panels).

Rationale: Anchored ramps make color regressions predictable (we can change an anchor and have a controlled, measurable delta across the UI). The micro-elevation system gives engineering an explicit mapping to CSS variables and hardware compositing expectations for low-latency render paths. The compact typography and spacing axes reduce layout thrash and token sprawl when building dense table rows and small chart annotations.

Risks:
- Breaking visual regressions in third-party embedded widgets.
- Slight increase in token count during transition period.
- Timeline risk: engineering work to wire aliases and provide runtime flags for compact mode must be completed before rollout.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge tokens to a feature branch with alias layer and runtime flag (engineers).
2) Offer a per-component opt-in in Storybook and the Console (design + dev) for verification.
3) Run accessibility contrast automation on key screens and the analytics dashboard.
4) Canary rollout to 5% of sessions for web Console with telemetry on layout regressions.
5) Full rollout after 2 weeks of Canary with no regressions and sign-off from Security and Accessibility.
acceptance_criteria: Token spec document published in Confluence with token definitions, rationale, and mapping table
Figma core file updated with token variables and compact component variants
Engineering feature branch creates CSS/JSON token output with alias layer and runtime compact flag
Automated contrast checks pass for neutral-accent combinations on primary dashboards
Storybook pages for Button, TableRow, ChartAnnotation show both regular and compact modes
Migration guide drafted with component-by-component instructions and deprecation timeline
migration_steps: Add alias layer: create semantic tokens that map to current primitives and new anchors
Expose runtime flag 'ui.compactMode' and wire to Storybook knobs for QA
Update Button, TableRow, ChartAnnotation components to reference semantic tokens rather than primitives
Run visual diff on all affected components and fix any edge-case where alias mapping produces unexpected spacing/overflow
Deprecate primitive tokens in a follow-up ticket with automated codemods where applicable
